senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced.; cmp. חֵפֶץ)desirable thing, beauty. Tanḥ.
units: <cite ref="Exodus 17">Mishp. 17</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Jeremiah 3:19">Jer. III, 19</cite>) <he>נחלת צבי … ארץ שנתאוו וכ׳</he> ‘an inheritance of choice’ …, a land which the kings of the world coveted.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 23:7">Num. R. s. 23</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Ezekiel 20:6">Ez. XX, 6</cite>, a. Jer. l. c.) <he>חביבה עלי ארץ וכ׳</he> the land of Israel is more precious to me than &c.—Pl. <he>צְבִיּוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 988:19">Yalk. Cant. 988</cite> <he>צְבִיּוֹתֵיהֶן</he>, v. infra.

<cite ref="Ketubot 112a:13">Keth. 112ᵃ</cite> (ref. to Jer. l. c.) <he>א״י נמשלה לצ׳ מה צ׳ וכ׳</he> the land of Israel is compared to a deer, as the skin of a deer (when once taken off) cannot again cover its body, so cannot Palestine contain its fruits; <cite ref="Gittin 57a:13">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="H00553"><he>חָזַק</he></cite>; Tanḥ. l. c.; a. e.—

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 7:13">Tosef. Sabb. VII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 8:13">VIII</cite>), 13 <he>פסק צ׳ את הדרך וכ׳</he> a deer cut the way off before me (a superstitious omen); <cite ref="Sanhedrin 65b:20">Snh. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>צ׳ הפסיקו בדרך</he> a deer cut him (me) off &c.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2:3:8">Y. Gitt. II, 44ᵇ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Tosefta Gittin 2:4">Tosef. ib. II, 4</cite> <he>כתבו על קרן של צ׳ וכ׳</he> if he wrote a letter of divorce on the horn of a deer, and cut it off and gave it to her.

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 13:2">Keth. XIII, 2</cite> <he>הניח מעותיו על קרן הצ׳</he> he has put his money on a deer’s horn, i.e. he cannot reclaim the unauthorized expense; a. fr.—Pl. <he>צְבָאִים</he>, <he>צְבָאִין</he>, <he>צְבָיִים</he>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 128a">Sabb. 128ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 14:8">Tosef. ib. XIV</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 15:8">XV</cite>), 8; Y. ib. XVIII, 16ᶜ, v. <cite ref="H01494"><he>חֲצָב</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 31:14">Gen. R. s. 31</cite>; a. fr.—Fem. <cite ref="R00038"><he>צְבִיָּה</he></cite>, <cite ref="R00042"><he>צְבִיָּיה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 988:19">Yalk. Cant. 988</cite> <he>למה … כצ׳ שרבתה צביותיהן וכ׳</he> why is Jochebed likened to a hind? Because she reared the beauties of Israel (Moses and Aaron); a. e.
